- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >72.5), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +2–3% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to counteract downward bias.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or weak; apply 0.8–1.2% upward bias for first 5–7 days.
- If recent 5-day average of true prices is > model forecast, model is lagging; adjust forecast to match 5-day moving average of true values.
- When sentiment spikes to 1.0+ and model forecasts rise sharply, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction; sentiment-driven volatility often overcorrects.
